reason:
The OBSERVATION is exactly right and I reproduced every part of it; the finding is refuted on its FIX, which is inert in two of its three edits and destructive in the third. Confirmed first: computed clip-path on .record resolves to inset(0px 0% 0px 0px) at 390/768/1280/1440, on both grounds, under ?motion=settled, ?motion=play after the 1.7s choreography, the webdriver default, and prefers-reduced-motion — the `both` fill of @keyframes draw sits in the animation origin, above the un-!important `[data-motion="settled"] .record { clip-path: none }` and its reduced-motion twin, so the clip is never lifted. .record's border box measures 1px tall (top 450.3, height 1 at 1440); .record-tag measures 433.3-448.1, wholly outside it. elementFromPoint across the tag's own width returns span.cols / span.colw / span.bar at every sample, never the tag. A pixel crop of the tag's rect is byte-identical-free: 871 bytes as shipped versus 2906 bytes with `.record { animation: none !important; clip-path: none !important }` — the crop is blank paper today and carries 'BEST WEEK · 8' with the override. The second-order claim is real too: with the clip lifted the tag paints under the twelfth column, because .cols follows .record in DOM order with no z-index between them, and the hatched partial bar (1227.3-1249.3) lands on the tag's 1162.3-1265 run and eats the '·'. The gates do not cover this — interaction-check.mjs line 520 only compares .record opacity early versus late, and says nothing about the tag reaching the screen. Severity stands: an unlabelled dashed rule across the hero chart reads by convention as a target or threshold, so the sighted owner is invited to conclude 'I am over the line' about a line that is not a target, while the .sr text tells the screen-reader user it is the previous best of 8. The eye gets strictly less than the ear, on the one comparison the movement exists to make.

Why it is nonetheless REFUTED: the proposed `padding-right: 96px` on .plot's .cols, .record and .gridline rules was measured under Playwright and it (a) does nothing at all where the seat says it does, (b) wrecks the chart where it does bite, and (c) carries a wrong number. On .record and .gridline the rules are position:absolute with left:0/right:0/height:0 under the file's global `* { box-sizing: border-box }` — padding cannot shorten a border-top, and both spans measured unchanged before and after (579-1265 at 1440, 41-349 at 390), so the dashed rule and the gridlines still run the full plot width exactly as before. On .cols (inset:0) it does bite, and the cost is severe: column width falls 53.5px to 45.5px at 1440 and 22px to 14px at 390 — a 36% loss of chart on the phone, where the twelve-column composition is a protected object — and every bar shrinks with it at 390 because the bar fills its column there. Worse, .xaxis is a separate flex row in .chart that gets no padding, so the ticks desynchronise from the columns they name: the twelfth column's centre moves 92px away from '13 JUL' at 1440 and 100.8px at 390, which turns a correct axis into a wrong one. And 96px does not even reserve enough — the tag measures 102.7px, so it would still overhang. A fix that leaves the stated target untouched, shrinks the protected phone composition by a third and mislabels the x-axis is worse than the defect it removes.

The first half of the seat's fix — take the tag out of the clipped box — is correct and is kept in sharpenedFix, with the seat's second half replaced and one mechanical omission repaired: --r is an inline custom property on .record, so a tag promoted to sibling inherits nothing and `bottom: calc(var(--r) * 1%)` would resolve to guaranteed-invalid. Re-file with the sharpened fix; this element is misleading-class and should not be allowed to close a round unfixed.
sharpenedFix: Two edits, no reserved gutter. (1) In chart(), emit the tag as a SIBLING of .record inside .plot and give it its own --r: `Best week · ${D.bestPrior}` — the inline --r must be repeated, it is not inherited from a sibling. (2) Replace the .record-tag rule with `position: absolute; left: 0; right: auto; bottom: calc(var(--r) * 1%); margin-bottom: 4px; color: var(--ink-3); background: var(--paper); padding-right: var(--gap-hair);`. Left, not right: the record sits at 8 and every historical column tops out at 7 or below, so the left end of the rule is clear paper while the right end is permanently under the twelfth column, which is the hatched partial bucket and a protected object that must not be knocked out by the label's paper background. Measured with this applied at 390/768/1280/1440: the tag hit-tests as itself at all ten sample points across its width, overlaps zero bars at every breakpoint, column width is unchanged (22 / 43.5 / 53.5 / 53.5), and the x-axis sync is unchanged from baseline. Do NOT add padding-right to .record or .gridline — it is provably inert on a zero-height left:0/right:0 box — and do NOT add it to .cols. If the entrance is still wanted, animate the tag's own opacity on its own delay rather than clipping its parent; and if the draw-in of the rule is to survive at all, either move `clip-path: none` to `!important` in BOTH the [data-motion="settled"] and prefers-reduced-motion blocks (the animation origin outranks a plain author declaration) or, better, move the animated clip off .record onto a `.record::before` carrying the border so nothing that must paint is ever inside a clipped box again.
breaks: The sharpened fix moves the label from the right edge to the left, so re-shoot light-full and light-partial at 390/768/1280/1440 on both grounds and re-run the frames set — the tag's paper background now knocks a ~103px hole in the LEFT end of the dashed rule instead of the right, which changes the read of where the record line starts. Re-check the .record-tag against .gridline b, which stays right-aligned: the two annotations now sit at opposite ends of the plot, and a reviewer must confirm that reads as deliberate (a named annotation at the start of its line, axis values at the axis) rather than as a stray. Re-run audit.mjs for AA contrast on ink-3 over paper at the new position — at 390 the tag now sits over the first four columns' airspace, and on the dark ground it sits over ground-2, a composite it did not previously cross. Re-run interaction-check.mjs: its .record opacity assertion at line 520 still passes, but if the entrance is re-authored as a tag-opacity animation the 'previous best draws last' check must be re-pointed at the tag, not the rule, or it will pass vacuously. Also re-verify the ?state=partial path, where chart({record:false}) emits neither element — the new sibling markup must not leave an orphan tag when record is false. Finally, re-capture at ?motion=play and confirm the tag's own delay still lands after the columns finish growing, since it no longer inherits .record's 1.1s delay through the clip.
